title: Berlin Museum Discounts - Quick Summary
items: **The second price on the board is the ermäßigt price, and at the state museums it is exactly half.** A 14 euro ticket at the Neues Museum, the Altes Museum, the Bode-Museum or the Gemäldegalerie becomes 7 euros with the right proof.

**Half price goes to students of any age, apprentices, pupils over 18, voluntary-service workers, jobseekers on ALG I, and severely disabled visitors** with a degree of disability of 50 or more. The card has to be in your hand, not in the hotel.

**Everyone under 18 is free at the state museums, not half price.** So are ICOM and press card holders, people on Bürgergeld or Grundsicherung, and a registered companion of a disabled visitor. Free visitors still collect a zero-euro ticket at the desk.
**There is no senior or pensioner rate.** A 70 year old pays the same 14 euros as a 40 year old, which surprises visitors from almost everywhere else in Europe.

**A pass is not a flat day.** The Museumsinsel-Ticket is 24 euros and the three-day Museumspass Berlin is 32, both halved with proof, but big temporary shows cost extra: until 27 September 2026 pass holders pay 6 euros more at the Alte Nationalgalerie.

**Not every museum follows the state rules.** The Berlinische Galerie charges 12 euros with a flat 7 euro reduction, and on the first Wednesday of the month everyone pays 7. Museumssonntag, the old free first Sunday, ended in December 2024.
